### F-255 — The coral edit test renamed the row docs.play.ts photographs

> _2026-09-24 · demo/blong-marine · resolved_

blong-suite CI failed on demo/blong-marine/test/docs.play.ts (Editor documentation images) with a
locator.click timeout after a 120s retry: the coral edit test of coral.play.ts had opened the first
row of the unfiltered browse table - the only row the marine database seeds, Staghorn Coral - and
renamed it, so the docs spec's fill("Staghorn") matched nothing. The rename persisted across runs
because coral is the one marine table that is not mocked (meta/db/db.ts mocks family, species and
habitat; marineCoralMerge.yaml seeds coralId 1), which is why the failure looked CI-only at first
and then became permanent in both local databases. Finding it needed three steps the tooling did not
make easy: blong-dev trace reads only 0-trace.trace and printed an empty timeline while the real
actions were in 1-trace.trace; the DOM snapshot resource was 594 bytes, so the evidence was a
screencast frame showing the tree polluted with test families; and the confirmation was SQL (coralId
1 renamed, its other fields still the seeded ones, because the edit test fills only editFields).

Lesson: createAndEditModel's search option exists precisely so the edit test does not take the first
row, and every other realm passes it (access, gateway, kopi) while the four marine specs did not. On
a page whose table declares widget.master the option is not enough on its own: the table renders the
navigator's selection, the navigator auto-selects its first loaded node by position, and a created
record outside that branch stays unreachable until its own node is selected (hence navigatorNode).
Selecting a node also had to stop being a toggle: PrimeReact reports a cleared selection when the
already-selected node is clicked again, and a navigator with no selection leaves the tables beside
it off the page entirely rather than showing everything (D-264).

Fixed: the coral and habitat specs pin their own record with createAndEditModel search (plus
navigatorNode for the coral page's navigator), the docs capture asserts the seeded row instead of
timing out, and the navigator no longer clears its selection (D-264). The family and species specs
keep the old behaviour, recorded as T-148.
